subject: Renewal proposal: term structure, ramp schedule & co-term options
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Bennett <julia.bennett@acmeworks.com>, Mike Ortiz <mike.ortiz@acmeworks.com>
Cc: contracts@acmeworks.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal kickoff & proposal: term structure, ramp schedule & co-term options

Hi Julia / Mike,

Thanks again for the partnership this past year — really glad the inference latency improvements made a difference for your recommendation engine. Our contract with Acme is up for renewal on 2026-04-15, and I wanted to summarize a clean proposal we think fits your expansion plans. High-level options below; attached is a short proposal PDF (proposal-redwood-2026.pdf).

Option A — 1-year (auto-renew, standard):
- Immediate capacity increase from 4 -> 8 dedicated units on Day 1.
- Price: list rate + 12% for added capacity.
- Auto-renews for additional one-year terms unless 60 days notice is provided.

Option B — 2-year ramp (recommended for predictable economics):
- Year 1: ramp to 6 units (month-by-month: +1 unit at months 1,3,6).
- Year 2: reach 10 units by month 12 and remain stable.
- Discount: 10% off year-1 unit rate, 15% off year-2 for committed capacity.
- Co-terming: we can align the Redwood renewal to your other platform contracts with a single annual co-term date (one-time adjustment).

Key asks from us to make this work:
- Sign a 24-month amendment for committed baseline units (we can structure overages as pay-as-you-go).
- A ramp schedule included in the amendment so invoicing/recognition is clear.

Questions for you: are you firm on a co-term date or would you prefer we co-term to your SAP/infra renewal on 2027-01-01? Also, any constraints from procurement around auto-renew?

If helpful I can loop in Vivek (AE) and Stephanie from CS to map the migration and capacity testing plan.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: proposal-redwood-2026.pdf

From: Julia Bennett <julia.bennett@acmeworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Ortiz <mike.ortiz@acmeworks.com>, contracts@acmeworks.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff & proposal: term structure, ramp schedule & co-term options

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear options. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

1) Procurement wants us to avoid automatic renewal unless there's an explicit opt-in; can Redwood offer opt-out language or a one-time immediate renewal notification instead?
2) We prefer co-terming with our infrastructure spend on 2027-01-01; can you align pricing/prorations to that date?
3) Engineering asked whether the ramp could be front-loaded (reach 8 units by month 4) instead of a long tail ramp — they have a major feature launch in Q3.

I attached a draft SOW for the launch and timelines (SOW-draft.docx). Procurement is on copy — if you can send a version with the exact amendment language, that would help speed review.

Julia
Director of Product Ops | Acme Works
julia.bennett@acmeworks.com

Attachments: SOW-draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal kickoff & proposal: term structure, ramp schedule & co-term options

Team — forwarding Julia's reply. Key asks: no automatic renewal (procurement requirement), co-term to 2027-01-01, and accelerate ramp to reach 8 units by month 4.

My proposal to keep economics healthy:
- Offer a 24-month committed amendment with a 12-month front-loaded ramp (6 units by month 2, 8 units by month 4), then step to 10 in year 2.
- Provide a one-time 10% ramp discount and a 12% committed discount on baseline for the 24-month term.
- Add an explicit auto-renew opt-out clause: renewal only if both parties sign; otherwise expiration on co-term date.

Attached is a quick model showing revenue impact and invoice phasing (pricing-model.xlsx). Can we confirm finance comfort and proposed contractual language for the opt-out clause? If so I will send a redline amendment to Acme.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal kickoff & proposal: term structure, ramp schedule & co-term options

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and model. Finance is OK with the 24-month committed structure but we need clear language for revenue recognition and overage billing:

- Contract should include a monthly scheduled ramp table in the amendment (units and committed spend per month). We will invoice based on the committed baseline for each month; any consumption above the committed units will be billed monthly as overage.
- For co-terming to 2027-01-01, include a proration schedule: first invoice after co-term adjustment will prorate to the co-term date so both sides have predictable invoices.
- Auto-renew: replace "auto-renew" with "renewal subject to mutual written agreement" and include a 60-day notice window if either party wants to renew on other terms. This satisfies procurement's opt-out requirement and keeps us flexible.

I can draft the contract paragraph and example ramp table — attaching a template. Also keep in mind ASC 606: multi-year commitments will recognize revenue in line with the committed schedule; ensure discounts are allocated across the term.

— Logan

Attachments: pricing-model.xlsx (v2)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Bennett <julia.bennett@acmeworks.com>, Mike Ortiz <mike.ortiz@acmeworks.com>, contracts@acmeworks.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal amendment and next steps (co-term, ramp schedule, opt-out)

Hi Julia / Mike / Acme Contracts team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on feedback. We've incorporated procurement and finance requests and attached a redline amendment (redwood-amendment-2026.pdf) for your review. Summary of the agreed structure below:

1) Term and co-term:
- 24-month committed amendment effective on execution.
- Co-term alignment to 2027-01-01 with proration on the first invoice post-execution so both parties hit the same annual date.

2) Ramp schedule (committed baseline):
- Month 0 (effective): 4 -> 6 units.
- Month 1: 6 -> 7 units.
- Month 3: 7 -> 8 units (so by month 4 you are at 8 units per engineering request).
- Month 12: step to 10 units baseline for year 2.

3) Pricing and discounts:
- 10% ramp discount applied to incremental units in months 0-3.
- 12% committed discount applied to baseline over the 24 months.

4) Auto-renew / opt-out:
- Renewal language changed to "renewal by mutual written agreement." If neither party executes a renewal by 60 days prior to the co-term date, the amendment expires and service continues on a month-to-month basis at standard rates.

5) Overage and invoicing:
- Overage billed monthly at pay-as-you-go rates above the committed monthly baseline.
- First invoice after co-term adjustment will be prorated to 2027-01-01 per finance template.

Next steps:
- If this looks good, please confirm by reply and I'll send the DocuSign link for signatures (link included below). We can target execution this week to align with your procurement timeline.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/to/redwood-acme-amendment
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line for your Q3 launch.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
